line: **Crocidura shrews:** the **Andaman White-toothed Shrew** (*C. andamanensis*), **Jenkin's Andaman Spiny Shrew** (*C. jenkinsi*) and the **Nicobar White-tailed Shrew** (*C. nicobarica*) are **endemic to India**; active at twilight or night, live in **leaf litter and rock crevices**; the White-toothed Shrew is found on **Mount Harriet**.

**NAQUIM:** CGWB's **National Aquifer Mapping and Management Programme** delineates aquifers and prepares **aquifer management plans**; its mappable area of about **25 lakh sq km** was reported completed in **2023**. Groundwater is regulated by the **CGWA**, constituted under the **EPA, 1986**.

mcq.s: The National Aquifer Mapping and Management Programme (NAQUIM) is implemented by which body?
mcq.x: NAQUIM is CGWB's programme to delineate aquifers and prepare aquifer management plans.

line: **Causes of extinction:** **deterministic processes** have cause and effect (glaciations, deforestation); **stochastic processes** are **random events** – unexpected weather changes, less food, more competitors, predators and parasites – acting alone or adding to deterministic effects.

mcq.s: Which of the following is an example of a stochastic process causing species extinction?
mcq.x: Stochastic processes are chance or random events such as unexpected weather changes; glaciation and deforestation are deterministic.

line: **Neonicotinoids:** a new class of insecticides chemically related to **nicotine** ("new nicotine-like insecticides"); they act on receptors in the **nerve synapse** and are far more toxic to **invertebrates (insects)**; discussed as a threat to **bees** (Colony Collapse Disorder).

line: **Himalayan Ibex:** a **subspecies of the Siberian (Asiatic) Ibex**, a wild goat; rocky, steep mountain zones of **J&K, Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh**; IUCN **NT**, WPA **Schedule I**.

**Neelakurinji:** the Kerala park that houses **Anamudi** (2,695 m) and the largest **Nilgiri tahr** population (Eravikulam) is famous for the **mass blooming** of the Neelakurinji flower; vegetation – high-altitude grasslands and sholas.

**Nilssonia softshell turtles:** freshwater turtles of South Asian rivers – **Burmese Peacock Softshell** (CR; Myanmar and **Karbi Anglong**, Assam), **Leith's Softshell** (CR; endemic to **peninsular rivers**), **Black Softshell** (CR; lower **Brahmaputra**, a few survive in a man-made pond in **Chittagong**).
**Barking Deer / Indian Muntjac:** omnivorous deer that **barks when frightened** by a predator, locally **Kaakad**; one of the **smallest deer**; native to South and SE Asia; IUCN **LC**.

**Gymnosperms:** e.g. **Cycas, Pinus, Gnetum** – ovules on the carpel surface, no ovary, style or stigma, so **no fruit**; **pine** is the largest family; **Gnetum and Cycas** are mostly confined to the **North-East, Eastern and Western Ghats and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**.
**Kannimara Teak:** in **Parambikulam Tiger Reserve** (Kerala) – one of the **oldest and largest living teak trees**; girth **6.48 m**, crown height 48.75 m, about **400 years** old.

**Pinguicula (Butterwort):** an insectivorous plant of the **alpine Himalayas, Kashmir to Sikkim**, growing along stream-sides in **cool boggy places**.

**GEEREF (Global Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy Fund):** a **Public-Private Partnership** funded by the **European Commission** and managed by the **European Investment Bank** (operational **2008**); a **fund of funds** investing in private-equity sub-funds for mitigation.

line: **Bioassays:** common in **pollution studies**, using any organism – **fish and insect bioassays** are most common; they find the **lethal concentration** or **effective concentration** of a pollutant causing mortality or other effects.
**Plasticulture:** use of plastic materials (**"ag plastics"**) in agriculture – soil fumigation film, **drip tape/tubing**, nursery pots and **silage bags**.

**Acclimation vs adaptation:** acclimation is a **short-term, individual-level** physiological, anatomical or morphological adjustment to environmental change; **adaptation** is the **genetic**, multi-generation change in a population.

line: **Acclimatization:** compensatory adjustment of an organism to environmental change in **natural (outdoor) conditions**, e.g. to **seasonal temperature** changes; plants acclimatize to rising **CO₂**, so the **CO₂-fertilization effect diminishes** over time.

**BIOFIN (Biodiversity Finance Initiative):** launched by **UNDP in 2012** to fill the **biodiversity finance gap** at the national level; helps implement the **National Biodiversity Action Plan** and National Biodiversity Targets; MoEFCC partners UNDP in it.

mcq.x: BIOFIN was launched by UNDP in 2012 to close the national biodiversity finance gap.

line: **Photooxidants (photochemical oxidants):** secondary pollutants – **ground-level ozone, PAN, hydrogen peroxide**, organic peroxides/aldehydes; strong **oxidising agents** causing eye and throat irritation, reduced lung function, **crop damage** and **rubber cracking**/fading of dyes.

**POPs:** most common are **organochlorine pesticides** – DDT, **Endosulfan, Chlordane, Endrin, Heptachlor**; also **hexachlorobenzene** (fungicide) and **PCBs**; they travel long distances, **bioaccumulate and biomagnify**.

**27 pesticides proposed for ban:** carcinogenic – **Oxyfluorfen**, Pendimethalin; endocrine disruptors – **Dicofol, Carbofuran**, Oxyfluorfen; in **2018** the Agriculture Ministry banned **18 Class I** pesticides but left out **Monocrotophos and Carbofuran**.
**Western Hoolock Gibbon:** the only **ape in India** (EN, Sch I); found in **Bangladesh, NE India and Myanmar west of the Chindwin River**, in tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests.
